encoding_finding.correction: M2a originally claimed these files are 'UTF-8 with CRLF, upstream original, byte-for-byte'. That was WRONG. The upstream git blobs are Shift-JIS + CRLF. The GitHub contents API silently transcoded them to UTF-8, and M2a vendored that transcoded copy.
encoding_finding.proof: git/trees/master?recursive=1 reports system/Utils.tjs = 3658 B / blob 529be2d212cb..., system/Initialize.tjs = 7246 B / blob 5da0a72cbd4a.... Fetching those blobs via /git/blobs/<sha> returns bytes that are NOT valid UTF-8 (0x83 at offset 20 is a Shift-JIS lead byte). The contents API copy is 3940 B / 8182 B and IS valid UTF-8.
encoding_finding.mapping_difference: GitHub's transcode uses CP932-style mapping (0x8160 -> U+FF5E FULLWIDTH TILDE, 0x817C -> U+FF0D FULLWIDTH HYPHEN-MINUS). Python's strict 'shift_jis' codec maps them to U+301C WAVE DASH / U+2212 MINUS SIGN. GalBox therefore tries CP932 before SHIFT_JIS in HostStreams.cpp.
encoding_finding.impact: Commercial KAG games ship Shift-JIS system/ scripts. The M2a self-test only exercised the UTF-8 transcode, so the Shift-JIS decode path had never really run. M2b adds a self-test over the original bytes.
